newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil INPC inflation index 9.12 pct in 1996 -- IBGE.
newsitem.headline: Brazil INPC inflation index 9.12 pct in 1996 -- IBGE.

text.p: Brazilian inflation in 1996 as measured by the National Consumer Prices Index (INPC) was 9.12 percent, the lowest level since the index was begun in 1979, the government's National Statistics Institute (IBGE) said.

The INPC is based on the spending of families earning up to eight times the minimum monthly wage of 112 reais (about $116.50). The Wider Consumer Price Index (IPCA), which gauges the spending of families earning up to 40 times the minimum, registered inflation of 9.56 percent last year, the lowest since the IBGE started to calculate the index, a statement said.
The IPCA index saw inflation of 0.47 percent last month, up from 0.32 percent in November.
The INPC result followed December inflation of 0.33 percent, a slight fall on the 0.34 percent registered in November.
